title: Accessibility
purpose: Can every user operate the page with keyboard, mouse, trackpad, touch, pen, a screen reader, and soon a TV remote, gamepad or voice? The axe run and manual screen-reader audit (PAP-73), the vision inspector (PAP-84) and the spec-conformance reviewer apply these items; serious failures are S1 by taxonomy.
scope: Rendered pages and components: DOM semantics, focus behaviour, names and roles, input modes, motion, forms, language. Design-system components (PAP-66 to PAP-74) are checked once in Storybook; pages are checked for how they compose them.
notCovered: Colour contrast measurement (visual rubric RUB-VIS-05 owns the number; a11y cites it).
Screen-reader testing on non-Linux platforms (PAP-156, blocked on runners).
Copy readability and plain-language review (docs rubric for docs; `question` for UI copy).

S0: The only way to confirm a payment is a drag gesture: the flow is impossible without a pointer (access-rule violation for keyboard and remote users).
S1: An icon-only button has no accessible name.
Focus is trapped inside a closed dialog, or lost to `body` on close.
A hover-only menu with no keyboard or touch path.
S2: A live region announces every keystroke of a search field.
Heading levels skip from h1 to h4.

items.title: Keyboard reachability and focus order
items.test: Can I reach and operate every control with Tab, Shift+Tab, arrows, Enter, Space and Escape in an order that matches the visual reading order, with no trap and no lost focus after an action?
items.verify: Keyboard-only replay (PAP-976); `tabindex` greater than 0 or on non-interactive elements in the diff; focus lands on the dialog heading on open and returns to the trigger on close.
items.falsePositives: Focus intentionally moved to a result region after a search, announced by a live region.

items.title: Name, role and value
items.test: Can I find an interactive element with no accessible name, a wrong role (clickable `div`), a state not exposed (`aria-expanded`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-selected`), or a name that differs from the visible label?
items.verify: axe `button-name`, `link-name`, `aria-*` rules (PAP-73); read the accessibility tree for changed components; visible label must be contained in the accessible name for voice users.
items.falsePositives: Decorative icons with `aria-hidden` next to a labelled control.

items.title: Visible focus
items.test: Can I tab to a control and not see where focus is, in any theme, including inside tables, canvases and custom controls?
items.verify: Screenshots with focus on each control kind in each theme; grep for `outline: none` without a replacement `:focus-visible` style.
items.falsePositives: Focus styles hidden for mouse users only via `:focus-visible`.

items.title: No hover-only or drag-only interaction
items.test: Can I find information or an action available only on hover (tooltips with actions, reveal-on-hover buttons) or only by dragging (reorder, resize, sliders) with no keyboard, touch or button equivalent?
items.verify: Trigger each hover reveal by focus and by tap; every drag has a menu or keyboard alternative (move up/down, resize handles with arrow keys); org standard: nothing hover-only or drag-only.
items.falsePositives: Hover previews that duplicate information available on click.

items.title: Pointer and touch input modes
items.test: Can I use the page with touch (no hover states, coarse pointer) and pen (pressure, hover without click) and find a control that needs a right click, a double click, a precise 1 px hit, or a scroll wheel?
items.verify: Playwright touch emulation on the phone widths; `pointer: coarse` media query respected; context-menu actions have a visible button equivalent.
items.falsePositives: Power-user shortcuts that duplicate a visible control.

items.title: Motion, timing and auto-updates
items.test: Can I find animation that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`, content that moves or updates without a pause control, a timeout that logs out without warning, or a toast that disappears before it can be read?
items.verify: Toggle reduced motion in the visual suite; toasts persist at least 5 s and are also logged in a notification list; session timeouts warn at least 60 s before.
items.falsePositives: Essential motion (progress indicators) that is also described in text.

items.title: Status messages and live regions
items.test: Can I complete an action (save, error, loading finished, presence change) and get no announcement, or so many announcements that the reader is unusable?
items.verify: `role=status` or `aria-live=polite` region receives one message per outcome; errors use `role=alert`; check the announcement text in the screen-reader transcript (PAP-73).
items.falsePositives: Silent background refreshes with no user-initiated action.

items.title: Forms: labels, errors and autocomplete
items.test: Can I find an input without a programmatic label, an error message not associated with its field (`aria-describedby`), a required field not marked, or a common field without `autocomplete`?
items.verify: axe form rules; submit an empty form and confirm focus moves to the first error and it is announced; `autocomplete` on name, email, address and card fields.
items.falsePositives: Search fields with a visible placeholder and an `aria-label`.

items.title: Language, direction and text scaling
items.test: Can I switch to Spanish and find `lang` unchanged on the document or a passage, or zoom text to 200 percent and lose content or controls?
items.verify: `html[lang]` follows the catalog locale; 200 percent zoom at 1280 px shows no overflow (visual RUB-VIS-01 at the equivalent width); RTL pseudo-locale run (PAP-688) where available.

items.title: Structure: landmarks, headings and tables
items.test: Can I navigate the page by landmarks and headings and find no `main`, skipped heading levels, a data table without headers, or a list built from `div`s?
items.verify: Accessibility tree of the page; one `h1`; `th` with `scope` on data tables produced by the table component; skip link to `main`.
items.falsePositives: Canvas and diagram surfaces that provide an equivalent list view.
